name: Boring Segments
description: You are given $$$n$$$ segments on a number line, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. The $$$i$$$-th segments covers all integer points from $$$l_i$$$ to $$$r_i$$$ and has a value $$$w_i$$$. You are asked to select a subset of these segments (possibly, all of them). Once the subset is selected, it's possible to travel between two integer points if there exists a selected segment that covers both of them. A subset is good if it's possible to reach point $$$m$$$ starting from point $$$1$$$ in arbitrary number of moves. The cost of the subset is the difference between the maximum and the minimum values of segments in it. Find the minimum cost of a good subset. In every test there exists at least one good subset.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$; $$$2 \le m \le 10^6$$$) — the number of segments and the number of integer points. Each of the next $$$n$$$ lines contains three integers $$$l_i$$$, $$$r_i$$$ and $$$w_i$$$ ($$$1 \le l_i \lt r_i \le m$$$; $$$1 \le w_i \le 10^6$$$) — the description of the $$$i$$$-th segment. In every test there exists at least one good subset.
output_specification: Print a single integer — the minimum cost of a good subset.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1555E — Boring Segments [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
